Retractable ratchet straps: Benchmark only. RHINO USA is about the only strap brand advertising at scale on Meta, so its ads show which hooks and offers work.
Windproof tarp clips: Anyone tarping a ute or trailer load buys these. Cheap, tiny and light to post, and rebought as clips get lost. Easy bundle with straps.
Anti-rattle hitch tightener: Every towing customer hates hitch rattle. Small, light, mid-price, and an easy upsell on a towing store.
Electric trailer dolly: Big-ticket sale to trailer and boat owners, so big profit per order. But heavy freight, more stock money tied up and harder returns.
Ute dash phone/tablet mount: Ute owners want it, but Uniden and GME already sell their own mounts at Supercheap and Repco.
Magnetic solar wireless trailer camera: Anyone towing a caravan, boat or trailer. Mid-price, light to ship, demos well in a video ad. Caravan stores mostly sell wired versions.
Wireless ute and trailer backup camera: Ute and trailer owners. Mid-price and light. Lots of cheap clones, so it needs a brand angle or a bundle to stand out.
Self-sealing tyre puncture repair: Tradies pick up screws on site constantly. Cheap, small, and used up, so people rebuy. Supercheap and Repco sell plug kits, so the price gap needs checking.
Portable smart key lock box: Tradies leaving keys for apprentices, clients or Airbnb guests. Small, mid-price, ships easily. Bunnings sells basic key safes, not smart portable ones.
8-tonne D-ring recovery shackles: Reference. Recovery buyers want rated gear, and ARB and others already own that in AU.
Concrete FormExtenders: Concreters buy for every job, so steady repeat orders. Trade-only niche: smaller market, but loyal buyers and little online competition.
Concrete step repair adhesive: Homeowners fixing crumbling steps. Cheap and quick to demo, but chemical shipping rules and lots of hardware-store alternatives.
Concrete chainsaw (ICS): Specialist pro machinery. High price, small market, dealer-style sale. Better as a supplier contact than a product.
Boulder Buddy rock lifter: Landscapers and machine owners moving rocks. Clear before/after demo and few rivals, but heavy steel to ship.
Clamp-on pallet forks: Farm and machinery owners turning a bucket into a forklift. Strong demo, but heavy freight and a smaller buyer pool.
Excavator split bushing shims: Excavator owners fixing worn bucket pins. Niche, but a repeat-buy part with very little online competition.
Skid steer tree saw: Machinery attachment, high ticket. Big profit per sale but a slow, dealer-style sell and heavy freight.
Battery fluid transfer pump: Farm and machinery owners refuelling from drums. Mid-price, practical, but this brand already sells in AU.
Touchless heavy machinery wash: Machinery and trailer owners. Used up, so customers rebuy. Liquid, so check freight and dangerous-goods rules.
POSTA solo post-setting tool: Reference. An Aussie tradie tool now selling in the US. Proof the market works both ways.
Rot-proof steel fence posts: Fencing material: heavy, bulky, low profit per kilo. A supply business, not an online store product.
Pump-free battery sprayer: Acreage, farm and garden owners. Mid-price and ships fine. Clear 'never pump again' demo for ads.
Shock-absorbing framing hammers: Carpenters who care about their tools. Premium brand, so it would need a distribution deal, not your own label.
Pro framer tool belt: Carpenters. Premium, made in the USA, needs a distribution deal and has sold in AU before.
Holsta adjustable tool belt: Every tradie wears a belt. Light, mid-price, good gift item. But an EU brand already selling widely.
Gripping tool roll and micro wrench: Small traffic and already ships to AU.
Modular tool organisers: Already in AU, patented, and Bunnings has a lookalike.
Chain-driven offset extension: Mechanics and tradies, small and light, but US interest is dropping.
90\u00b0 precision track saw guide: Carpenters and DIY builders. Mid-price, but the brand already sells on Amazon AU.
Precision oil-based marker (Precisq): Every tradie uses markers and keeps losing them. Tiny, cheap to post, constantly rebought. Great add-on, low profit on its own.
Precision-tip quick-dry marker: Same as above: a cheap consumable that brings repeat orders.
Multi-size marking scriber: Carpenters and fabricators. Small, light, low cost. Good add-on, not a hero product.
MeasurePro tape, laser and level in one: Already cheap on eBay and AU stores.
Reekon T1R hybrid measuring tool: Premium gadget for carpenters. Needs a deal with the brand; can't be your own label.
Moasure 2 Pro area measurer: Landscapers, fencers and concreters quoting jobs. Premium brand, likely already in AU.
Laser tape measure ruler: Similar products already cheap in AU.
Automatic wire stripper: Electricians and scrap recyclers. Higher ticket, clear demo. Niche buyer.
Tool-free LED strip and wire connectors: Ute and caravan owners wiring lights. Cheap consumable add-on, lots of clones.
DIY pipe threading tool: Plumbers and DIY. Check AU (BSP) thread standards before anything else.
Conduit bender: Electricians. Niche, and AU conduit sizes differ from the US.
Welding gear and hoods: Welders. Established brand with 6,000+ reviews; it would need a distribution deal.
Custom welding hoods: Welders who like custom gear. A design brand play: strong on social media, but you'd need your own designs.
Metal repair glue (cold weld): Farmers, mechanics, ute owners. Ad has run 450 days so demand is proven, but chemical shipping and JB Weld at Bunnings.
Laser rust cleaner: Big-ticket machine for fabricators. Laser safety rules in AU. A different business.
Low-temperature metal repair rods: Cheap fix-it add-on. Demos well, but quality needs testing before selling.
Cabinet door hanging jig: Cabinet makers and renovators. Small and light; the current seller ships slowly to AU, which leaves room for a local stockist.
Solo door hanging tool: Builders hanging doors alone. Only selling in Europe so far, so the US and AU are untested.
Door lock installation kit: Carpenters and handymen. Small and light; check AU lock bore sizes.
Contour gauge with lock: Floor layers and tilers. Cheap; Bunnings has basic versions.
Self-adhesive floor transition strip: Renovators. Cheap, and Bunnings sells transition strips.
Diamond hole saw for tile and glass: Tilers and plumbers. Used up, so rebought, but Bunnings sells them.
Stainless plasterboard patch clips: Only works as part of a repair kit.
Liquid Rubber deck and roof sealant: Ad has run 936 days, the longest on the list. Homeowners and caravan owners. Liquid freight needs checking.
Deck stain brush pole: Homeowners and deck builders. Light and cheap to post. Seasonal.
Composite decking: Building material sold through dealers. A different business.
Solar automatic gate opener: Rural and acreage owners. Mid-to-high ticket, good profit per sale. Needs AU electrical compliance.
Concrete crack filler sealant: Homeowner DIY. Cheap, chemical shipping rules, lots of alternatives.
Custom-moulded earplugs: Tradies on loud sites. Brand already sold in AU.
Stylish safety glasses: SafeStyle (an AU tradie brand) owns this.
Rechargeable work headlamp: Every tradie and ute owner needs one. Light, cheap to post, good add-on and gift item. Crowded, so it needs a hook.
Wearable Bluetooth speaker for site: Tradies on sites that ban earbuds. Mid-price, unusual product, check AU site safety rules.
Pitch Hopper roof tool: Roofers and Christmas-light installers. Niche, seasonal; check working-at-heights rules.
Magnetic 1,800-lumen work light: Every tradie and ute owner. Light, cheap to post, good gift item. Bunnings sells magnetic lights, so check the price gap.
Steel glove clamp for tool belts: Every tradie with gloves. Tiny, cheap to post, impulse buy. Great add-on, low profit on its own.
Steel-hook heavy-duty work suspenders: Tradies with heavy tool belts. Mid-price, light, clear problem. Bunnings only sells basic clip braces.
DIY spray foam insulation kit: Builders and DIY renovators. Hazardous freight and AU labelling rules. Only worth it as part of a building-materials line.
Merino work socks with 10-year guarantee: Every tradie in boots. Wears out, so customers come back. Flat and light, so very cheap to post.
Cooling hi-vis sun work shirt: Outdoor workers in an Aussie summer. Strong fit, but must meet the AU hi-vis standard, and clothing means sizes and returns.
Adjustable door hinge mortise jig: Carpenters and handymen. Small, light, cheap; check Amazon AU for clones.
15\" curved reciprocating saw blade: Used up, so rebought, and very cheap to post. FixionTools already gets 19% of its traffic from AU.
4-way panel glue-up clamp: Cabinet makers and woodworkers. Heavier steel, so check freight and SpeTool's AU pricing.
Angle-grinder drill bit sharpener: Any tradie with drill bits. Ad has run 451 days, so demand is proven, but it's a cheap clone item and Temu has it.
LockNFlate pro retractable air and water: Reference. An Aussie-made workshop brand selling to US tradies on Facebook.
